bigPicture.subtitle: Jesus Is Better — So Hold Fast
paragraphs: Picture a community of believers who once burned with faith. When they first believed, they suffered for it: they were publicly insulted, some were imprisoned, and their property was seized. They took it joyfully. “For you both had compassion on me in my chains, and joyfully accepted the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you have for yourselves a better possession and an enduring one in the heavens” (Hebrews 10:34). But years have passed. The pressure has not let up, the Lord has not yet returned, and some are growing tired. Their ears have become dull. Some have stopped meeting with the church. And many are being pulled back toward the familiar world of the old covenant — the temple, the priests, the sacrifices — which looked so solid and safe.

Into that situation comes the letter to the Hebrews. Its writer calls it a “word of exhortation” (Hebrews 13:22): a sermon written down. It does not open with a greeting but with a fanfare: “God, having in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets at many times and in various ways” (Hebrews 1:1), “has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son” (Hebrews 1:2). From there it shows, step by step, that Jesus is greater than everything the readers were tempted to go back to: greater than the angels, than Moses, than Joshua, than Aaron and the whole priesthood, than the old covenant, the tabernacle and its sacrifices.

The key word is ‘better’. Jesus is “so much better than the angels” (Hebrews 1:4). He is “the collateral of a better covenant” (Hebrews 7:22) and “the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises has been given as law” (Hebrews 8:6). Believers have a better hope, better sacrifices, a better possession, a better country and a better resurrection. Everything in the old covenant was a shadow; Christ is the substance. To go back would be to swap the reality for the picture.

And the key command is ‘hold fast’. Woven through the teaching are five solemn warnings and many encouragements. “let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for he who promised is faithful” (Hebrews 10:23). Hebrews is written for anyone who is weary, discouraged or tempted to drift. It shows you Jesus — your great High Priest, who understands your weakness and lives forever to intercede for you — and calls you to run your race with endurance, “looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith” (Hebrews 12:2).

bridge.intro: The Holy Spirit placed Hebrews after Paul's letters. (Philemon, the short personal letter that stands between Titus and Hebrews, will be added to this study once its text has been re-fetched.) Titus ended by pointing ahead to Hebrews, and the connections are rich.

points.title: From ‘Our Great God and Savior’ to ‘The Radiance of His Glory’
points.body: Titus called Jesus “our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ” (Titus 2:13). Hebrews opens by showing what that means: “His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power” (Hebrews 1:3). The Son is God's final word, the heir of all things, the one through whom the worlds were made, worshipped by angels and addressed by the Father as God (1:8). No book of the Bible sets out the greatness of Christ more fully.

points.title: From ‘Purify for Himself a People’ to ‘Purified Us of Our Sins’
points.body: Titus said that Christ gave Himself to “purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works” (Titus 2:14). Hebrews explains how He did it: “when he had by himself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high” (Hebrews 1:3). He is both the High Priest and the sacrifice. He entered the true holy place “through his own blood” and obtained “eternal redemption” (Hebrews 9:12).

points.title: From a Letter by Paul to a Sermon by an Unknown Preacher
points.body: Titus opened with Paul's name. Hebrews names no author. Early Christians suggested Paul, Barnabas, Apollos or Luke, but the letter itself does not say, and its writer says he received the gospel from those who heard the Lord (2:3), which Paul insisted he did not. The honest answer is that we do not know who wrote it. What we do know is that it was written by a gifted teacher who knew Timothy (“Know that our brother Timothy has been freed” (Hebrews 13:23)) and that the church received it as Scripture. Its authority rests on its message, not on its author's name.

points.title: From ‘Zealous for Good Works’ to ‘Provoke One Another to Love and Good Works’
points.body: Titus ended with a call for believers to be “careful to maintain good works” (Titus 3:8). Hebrews carries this into the life of a struggling church: “Let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good works” (Hebrews 10:24), not forsaking meeting together. And it closes with practical commands about love, hospitality, marriage, money and leaders (Hebrews 13). The doctrine of Christ's greatness always leads to the practice of love.

coreTheme.title: Jesus Is Better — So Hold Fast
paragraphs: The whole letter alternates between teaching and exhortation. The teaching shows that Jesus is better. He is better than the angels, because He is the Son (chapters 1–2). He is better than Moses, because Moses was a servant in God's house and Jesus is the Son over it (chapter 3). He gives a better rest than Joshua could give (chapters 3–4). He is a better High Priest than Aaron, a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek (chapters 5–7). He mediates a better covenant, serves in a better sanctuary, and offers a better sacrifice — Himself, once for all (chapters 8–10).

The exhortation follows from the teaching: so hold fast. “Having then a great high priest, who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold tightly to our confession” (Hebrews 4:14). Because He was tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin, “Let us therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace for help in time of need” (Hebrews 4:16). The great ‘therefore’ of chapter 10 calls believers to draw near, hold fast and encourage one another.

The warnings are serious. Hebrews says that those who neglect “so great a salvation” (Hebrews 2:3) will not escape; that an evil, unbelieving heart can lead to “falling away from the living God” (Hebrews 3:12); and that there is no other sacrifice for those who deliberately reject Christ. This study will not soften those passages. But they are written to people the writer is “persuaded of better things” about (6:9). The warnings are a loving shout to people near a cliff edge.

And the goal is endurance with eyes on Jesus. Chapter 11 parades the heroes of faith who lived by promises they had not yet received. Chapter 12 turns from them to Him: “looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross” (Hebrews 12:2). Faith is not a leap into the dark but a steady fixing of the eyes on the One who has already run the race and finished it.

truths.intro: As we journey through these 13 chapters, the Holy Spirit wants to anchor these truths in your spirit:

items.title: God Has Spoken His Final Word in His Son
items.body: God spoke in many ways through the prophets, but in these last days He has spoken by His Son. There is no greater revelation to wait for. Everything God wants you to know about Himself, His salvation and His purposes is found in Jesus. To hear Him is to hear God; to neglect Him is to neglect the greatest salvation.

items.title: You Have a Great High Priest Who Understands
items.body: “For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin” (Hebrews 4:15). Jesus knows weakness, pain and temptation from the inside. He lives forever to intercede for you, so you can come to God's throne boldly, not to be condemned but to receive mercy and grace in your time of need.

items.title: Faith Endures by Looking to Jesus
items.body: “Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen” (Hebrews 11:1). The heroes of faith lived for a better country they never saw on earth. Faith keeps going when the promise is delayed and the road is hard, because it is fixed on God's faithfulness and on Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy set before Him.

preparation.intro: Before we step into Chapter 1, prepare your spirit with these reflections:

items.title: Where Are You Drifting?
items.body: Hebrews warns against drifting away — not a sudden fall, but a slow slide caused by inattention. Honestly consider: is your love for Christ as warm as it was? Are you meeting with other believers, listening to God's word, praying? Name any area where you have been drifting, and ask God to draw you back as you read.

items.title: What Are You Tempted to Go Back To?
items.body: The first readers were tempted to go back to a religion of ritual that felt safer than following Jesus through suffering. What ‘old ways’ attract you — a comfortable religion without cost, a past life, a reliance on your own performance? As you read, let the writer show you that Jesus is better than all of them.

prayerOfActivation: “Father, You have spoken in many ways through the prophets, and in these last days You have spoken to me by Your Son. Open my ears to hear Him. Let me see Jesus as He is: the heir of all things, the radiance of Your glory, the exact imprint of Your nature, who upholds all things by His powerful word and who purified me from my sins. Show me that He is better than every angel, every leader, every ritual and every comfort I might be tempted to go back to. Keep me from drifting away and from a hard, unbelieving heart. Thank You for my great High Priest, who understands my weakness and was tempted in every way as I am, yet without sin. Give me boldness to draw near to Your throne of grace and receive mercy and help in my time of need. Make me hold fast to my confession without wavering, because You who promised are faithful. Give me endurance to run the race You have set before me, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of my faith. In the mighty name of Jesus, Amen!”
